Implementation Plan

Plan for #8952: skip the full review when the current head already had a clean review

Planning ref: `main` @ `f9d5c7a3fdaeb0b57a4665c99dd96d1289a072c2`. The "Integration branch mismatch" line reads `unknown`, not `true`, so planning continues. The clarify phase auto-answered this issue and asked no questions. The issue body records an earlier user decision (Q8: A) that `force-review` does not bypass the new skip; the plan follows it.

## Files likely to change
- `scripts/review_autofix_step_evaluate_gate.sh`
- `scripts/review_autofix_step_post_editor_summary.sh`
- `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml`
- `tests/test_review_autofix_clean_same_head_gate.py` (new)
- `tests/test_review_freshness_ci_failed.py`
- `README.md`
- `agents.d/8952-clean-same-head-skip.md` (new)
- `changelog.d/8952-skip-clean-same-head-review.md` (new)

## Automation (§20.E)
- **Scripts:** no new script. This extends the gate script and the editor-summary script.
- **Entry point:** unchanged. The gate step (`id: evaluate`, gate job of `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml`) runs on every review run, whatever dispatched it:
  - the `review_autofix_sweep.yml` `*/30` cron
  - `_dispatch_review_for_conflicts` in the poller
  - `review_merge_train.sh release`
  - `provider_outage.py` resume
  - `pull_request` events through `internal-review.yml` and consumer `ai-review.yml`, which reach the gate via `@stable`
- **Long-running supervisor:** none.
- **DB work:** none.
- **`docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`:** no entry, because there is no new script.

## Functions or modules to implement

### 1. `scripts/review_autofix_step_evaluate_gate.sh`

**a. Base SHA from the existing PR read (line ~88).**
- Add `base_sha: (.base.sha // "")` to the existing `/pulls/{n}` `--jq` object. This adds no API call.
- Parse it into a new `pr_base_sha_gate` (declared next to `pr_base_ref_gate`, ~line 49), lower-cased, and kept only if it is 40 hex characters.
- In the retarget block (~line 140), clear `pr_base_sha_gate=""` alongside `pr_mergeable=""`. A retarget means the fetched base no longer applies.
- In the output block (~line 1385), add `echo "base_sha=${pr_base_sha_gate}" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"`.

**b. Extend the comment fetch in `gate_fetch_marker_comments` (lines 343-346).** This stays the same single paginated call (§14).
- In the existing `select(...)`, add `or ($b | contains("<!-- review-autofix-clean:v1 "))` **before** the freshness clause. `tests/test_review_freshness_ci_failed.py:148` pins the substring `or ($b | contains("<!-- ai:freshness-ci-failed:v1 "))) |`, and inserting earlier keeps it intact.
- Change the program from `[ <existing> ]` to `[ <existing> ] + [ .[] | select((.user.type // "") != "Bot") | {id: .id, author_login: (.user.login // ""), author_type: (.user.type // ""), author_association: (.author_association // ""), created_at: (.created_at // ""), body: "", activity_only: true} ]`.
  - These slim records have no body, so nothing a human wrote leaves GitHub's response.
  - The existing `jq -s 'add // []'` still merges the pages.
  - Every existing consumer reads markers from `body`: the partial filter (~421), the fingerprint-cap helper (~626/667), the consumer at ~858, the freshness check (~1250) and the skip-notice dedupe (~1328). An empty body matches none of them. The implementer must confirm this for the ~858 consumer.
- Update the cost comment above the function: one call; the file now also holds slim non-Bot activity records.

**c. New "Clean same-head skip" block, placed right after the terminal same-head block (after line ~546) and before the fingerprint cap.**

It reuses the terminal block's structure: shell preconditions, then `gate_fetch_marker_comments`, then an inline `python3 - <<'PY'` parser whose first comment line is unique and greppable (`# Decide whether the newest trusted review-autofix-clean:v1 marker ...`), then KEY=VALUE output read with `awk`.

Shell preconditions, all required; none of them makes an API call:
- `SHOULD_RUN=true`
- `AUTOFIX_SKIP_CLEAN_SAME_HEAD` (default `true`) is not `false`
- `FORCE_RB_JUDGE` is not `true`. This also covers security-hold follow-ups: `review_security_hold_sweep.py` dispatches them with `force_rb_judge=true`.
- the PR number is numeric
- `pr_base_retargeted` is not `true`
- the event is not `pull_request` with `EVENT_ACTION=reopened` (decision D2)
- `pr_mergeable=true`
- `pr_head_sha_gate` and `pr_base_sha_gate` are 40 hex characters

Logging when the block is reached:
- If a precondition fails, log `AUTOFIX_GATE_CLEAN_SAME_HEAD_CHECK outcome=no_skip reason=<disabled|force_rb_judge|base_retargeted|reopened|mergeable_not_true|head_sha_unavailable|base_sha_unavailable> pr=<n> head_sha=<sha|unknown>`.
- If the switch is off, log nothing beyond that one line.

The `[force-review]` title marker and the `force-review` label are **not** checked here (Q8: A). They keep bypassing `terminal_same_head` and the deterministic skip exactly as today.

The Python parser:
- **Inputs (env):** `CLEAN_MARKER_COMMENTS_FILE` (the gate comments file), `GATE_HEAD_SHA`, `GATE_BASE_SHA`, `GATE_SUPPORT_SHA="${REVIEW_SUPPORT_SHA:-}"`, `GATE_PR_NUMBER`, `GATE_MARKER_AUTHOR_LOGIN="${gate_marker_author_login}"`.
- **Trusted marker:** a comment counts only if all of these hold:
  - its author login (case-insensitive) equals the marker author login;
  - its body starts with `AI autofix editor summary`;
  - its **last non-empty line** fully matches `^<!-- review-autofix-clean:v1 head=([0-9a-f]{40}) base=([0-9a-f]{40}) support=([0-9a-f]{40}|none) run=([0-9]+) -->$`.

  The last-line rule stops a fake marker that LLM editor output places mid-comment, because the writer always appends the real marker last. Comments that contain the token but fail to parse are counted as `malformed_markers`.
- **Newest marker for this head:** the newest trusted marker by `(created_at, id)` whose `head` equals the current head.
- **Decision order** (the first matching rule wins; `skip` only if none matches):
  1. no trusted marker for this head → `no_skip reason=no_marker`
  2. marker `base` differs from the current base → `base_moved`
  3. marker `support` differs from the current support SHA (`none` matches only an empty current SHA) → `support_changed`
  4. any trusted comment whose body matches `<!-- ai:freshness-ci-failed:v1 pr=<n> head=<head> -->` at any time → `freshness_ci_failed`. Same regex as gate line ~1253.
  5. a trusted comment newer than the marker that carries a `review-autofix-failure:v1 head=<head>` marker, or a `REVIEW_AUTOFIX_PARTIAL_V1` block with `head_sha=<head>` → `newer_failure_marker`. This covers provider-outage recovery: `provider_outage.py` dispatches with no distinguishing input, but it only resumes PRs whose newest decisive marker is an outage failure. It also covers a clean run that failed after its summary was posted.
  6. any record newer than the marker by `(created_at, id)` whose author is not the marker author and whose `author_type` is not `Bot` → `newer_human_comment`
  7. otherwise `candidate`
- **Output:** `decision`, `reason`, `marker_run`, `marker_comment_id`, `matching_markers`, `untrusted_markers`, `malformed_markers`, each value cleaned to `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]`.
- Malformed JSON or a non-list input exits 2.

Reviews check, only when the parser returns `candidate`:
- One `gh api --paginate -X GET "repos/${REPOSITORY}/pulls/${PR_NUMBER}/reviews" -f per_page=100 --jq '[.[] | {id: .id, author_login: (.user.login // ""), author_type: (.user.type // ""), submitted_at: (.submitted_at // ""), state: (.state // "")}]' | jq -c -s 'add // []'`. A comment above the call explains that the gate has no reviews fetch, that this runs only when a matching clean marker exists, and that it costs at most one paginated call (§14).
- A review with a non-empty `submitted_at` ≥ the marker's `created_at`, from an author who is neither the marker author nor a `Bot`, gives `no_skip reason=newer_review`.
- Pending reviews (no `submitted_at`) are ignored.
- To support this, the parser also prints `marker_created_at`, cleaned to `[0-9TZ:-]`.

Results:
- **Skip:** set `SHOULD_RUN="false"`, `SKIP_REASON="clean_same_head"` and `GATE_SKIP_RECORDED="true"`, and echo exactly `AUTOFIX_GATE_SKIP reason=clean_same_head pr=<n> head_sha=<sha> marker_run=<id> marker_comment_id=<id>`. This is the same output path `terminal_same_head` uses. No job or step in the workflow special-cases `skip_reason == 'terminal_same_head'`; the implementer should grep `skip_reason ==` to re-confirm. A skip posts no comment.
- **No skip:** echo `AUTOFIX_GATE_CLEAN_SAME_HEAD_CHECK outcome=no_skip reason=<r> pr=<n> head_sha=<sha> matching_markers=<k> untrusted_markers=<k> malformed_markers=<k>`.
- **Errors:** `gate_marker_fetch_state` is not `ok`, the marker author is unavailable, the parser exits non-zero or prints nothing, or the reviews GET fails. Each logs `AUTOFIX_GATE_CLEAN_SAME_HEAD_CHECK outcome=error reason=<comments_api_error|marker_author_unavailable|parse_error|reviews_api_error> pr=<n> head_sha=<sha>`, and the run continues normally (fail open).

### 2. `scripts/review_autofix_step_post_editor_summary.sh`

Add a block after the sandbox-excluded block (after line ~257) that builds `clean_marker_suffix=""`. It is set only when all of these hold:
- `editor_summary_is_real=1` (a real summary, not the fallback path at ~138);
- `sandbox_excluded_nothing_committed=1` (positive evidence of no commit) and `DID_COMMIT` is not `true`;
- the change status parsed from `EDITOR_SUMMARY_FILE` is `not-edited`. Use a status-only awk that reuses the same section-header regex as the existing awk; the existing awk stays untouched;
- `sandbox_excluded_marker_suffix` is empty and `${sandbox_excluded_findings:-0}` is `0`. Any sandbox-excluded finding is a failure path, even when its marker was unavailable;
- `AUTOFIX_FAILURE_HEAD_SHA` and the new `AUTOFIX_CLEAN_MARKER_BASE_SHA` are 40 hex characters after lower-casing;
